steps: Raise your dominant hand to chest height in front of your torso.
Sweep the hand backward in a smooth arc that passes over your dominant shoulder.
Let the hand travel well behind the shoulder so the backward motion clearly reads as the past.
Keep your palm facing your body for the entire movement.
Make the arc larger and more emphatic when you mean long ago — a bigger sweep means further back.
tip: One backward sweep over the shoulder says PAST; a bigger, more emphatic arc means 'long ago'.

steps: Make an H handshape with both hands, extending the index and middle fingers together and folding the rest down.
Hold your non-dominant H hand steady in front of you with the palm facing down.
Bring your dominant H hand beside it so the fingertips of both hands nearly touch.
Move the dominant hand outward in a small double motion, as if marking off a short length.
Keep the motion compact — one quick, large outward sweep would mean BRIEF instead.
Stay neutral-faced; this sign works for short lengths and short durations alike.
tip: Lifeprint teaches two SHORTs: H hands for short-in-length or duration (this entry), and a hand bent at the knuckles for short-in-height.

steps: Raise your dominant hand to chest height in front of you.
Extend all five fingers and spread them wide apart to open the whole hand.
Turn your palm to face back toward you when signing the number in isolation.
When counting in a series, turn the palm to face forward instead.
Hold the open hand still with a neutral face — number signs carry no extra movement.
tip: Five fingers spread wide with the palm facing you — the mirror of the /numbers/5.svg illustration on the site.
